title: Alleviating Drug Shortages: The Role of Mandated Reporting Induced Operational Transparency
authors: Jung-Hee Lee; Hyun Seok Lee; Hyoduk Shin; Vish Krishnan
eligible_reason: One adoption date per regression. Table 1: Canada's 2017 mandatory-reporting rule vs US (treat##after), shortage-incident level with year-month and therapeutic-category FE, no unit FE, a single treated cohort. Table 2: US-only pre/post FDASIA 2012 (post_FDA) with no untreated comparison group, interacted with competition categories, covariates and manufacturer x year FE. Both US (2012) and Canada (2017) adopt, but they are never pooled into a staggered design; US is already treated throughout the Canada sample.
design_notes: Code_Table1_2.do. Table 1: reg ttr i.treat##i.after i.inject i.year_month i.therapeutic_category2, vce(robust) on ds_US_canada_random_sample.csv (2017-2018). Table 2: reg logdiff i.post_FDA ... i.year#i.labelernamex2 and reghdfe days_shortage i.post_FDA##comp_type ..., on ds_US_random_sample.csv (2010-2015).
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Within each analysis one policy date (Canada 2017 in Table 1; US 2012 in Table 2).
excluded_specs_summary: Table 1 col 1: single-cohort 2x2 without unit FE; cols 2-5: single-group pre/post, trend tests, collapsed. Table 2 / Figures 3, 5: US pre/post with no control group, competition interactions, CEM iweights in Figure 5 variants.
